dedupe_keys.name: succurro national directory of us help and support services food assistance shelter free clinics crisis lines and more

description: This directory lists where people in the United States can find help, such as food banks and food assistance, shelters, free clinics, crisis lines and treatment services, down to the town where each is offered. The producer is Kara Zajac, who assembled it from federal open data from agencies including SAMHSA, HRSA, the Department of Veterans Affairs, HUD and USDA, and from open community directories. Coverage is about 257,000 records: 12,950 organisations, 136,526 service locations and 74,790 recurring support meetings across 32,307 places, each citing its source and the date it was last checked. The release ships with a JSON schema, a validation step, a statement of which sources were excluded for rights reasons, and an export in the Open Referral HSDS 3.0 standard. It is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 licence, with a website and repository. Caveats: a single-person project, commercial use is not allowed, and service hours and eligibility change faster than releases. Simulation uses: locating food assistance and shelter capacity for disaster and emergency planning, and measuring access to safety-net services for vulnerable populations. Related records: the USDA Food Access Research Atlas (data-usda-ers-food-access-research-atlas) maps food access, and the New York retail food stores (data-nys-retail-food-stores) list food outlets.
